segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Good afternoon, distinguished colleagues, to the Secretary of the Department of Information

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: and Communications Technology, the heads and officials of the National Telecommunications

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Commission, the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center, the National Privacy

segments.text: Commission, as well as other officials and representatives joining us here today.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Today, we take up the fiscal year 2027 National Expenditures Program of the Department of

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: We assess this budget at an important juncture for the country. In just a few years, the government has built

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: a stronger legal foundation for a connected Philippines. The E-Governance Act advances

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: digital government and integrated public services. The Conectadong Pinoy Act seeks to expand access

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: and competition in data transmission and connectivity. But passing laws is only the

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: beginning. This budget must turn those laws into actual service. For me, the first test remains

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: connectivity. We will therefore be looking closely at the connectivity targets presented to Congress.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: We want to know not only how many sites, access points, kilometers of fiber, or institutions are

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: reported as connected, but whether or not people on the ground are actually receiving reliable,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: This is particularly important for our public schools. Connectivity in schools should mean more

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: than being able to just say that the school has been connected. We have to ask, is the connection

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: actually working? Is the bandwidth sufficient for teachers and students? Is it reliable throughout

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: the school day and cannot support digital learning, online government systems, and increasing

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: In short, we have to validate whether our target translates into real connectivity.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Our challenge is not just how many sites are connected to the report. The question is whether

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: teachers and students use it every day. And as we connect more Filipinos, we must also confront a

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Where does our data go? Who controls the infrastructure carrying it? And how well are we

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: protecting it? Data sovereignty is no longer an abstract technological issue. Government is

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: digitizing records, transactions, identities, payments, and public services. We're generating

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: and processing enormous amounts of sensitive government data, citizen data. And so we need

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: to understand where critical government data is stored.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: We need to understand where infrastructure is, what infrastructure carries it, and what safeguards apply when cloud and data services are provided by foreign entities and whether government has adequate control over information that is critical to national security and public administration.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: This brings us to the expanding role of the DICT. The Department can no longer be viewed as a simple government agency responsible for internet connectivity and information technology projects.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: In this new age, DICT sits at the intersection of connectivity, cybersecurity, artificial

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: intelligence, digital government, data governance, transparency, and economic development.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Every government system we put online creates both an opportunity for better public service

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: The question for this committee is whether we are investing enough, not only in systems

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: but in people, defenses, standards, and institutions to protect them.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: AI can make government faster and more efficient.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: It can support education, health, disaster response, agriculture, business, and many

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: But government must also be prepared for its risks.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: to privacy issues, cybersecurity, accountability, and the possible disruption of Filipino jobs.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Our approach cannot simply be to fear AI or to regulate it without understanding.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: The Philippines should be positioning itself to use AI, govern AI responsibly, and create

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: opportunities for Filipinos in AI-driven economies.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: The same digital transformation should strengthen transparency.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Technology should make government easier to scrutinize, not harder.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Digital systems should allow citizens to know how public money is spent, how government

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: decisions are made, and whether agencies are delivering what they promised.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: If we are spending billions of pesos to digitize the government, the greater accountability

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: and transparency should be among the returns of that investment.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Reliable broadband, competitive digital infrastructure, cloud services, cybersecurity, data centers,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: digital platforms, and emerging technologies can attract investment and create higher-value

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Our objective should not be to just make Filipinos consumers of technology.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: We should be building conditions for Filipinos to become developers, cybersecurity experts,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: engineers, entrepreneurs, innovators, and creators of technology.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Ang digital transformation ay hindi lang tungkol sa mas mabilis na internet.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Dapat may trabaho, negosyo, oportunidad at mas mahusay na serbisyo na kasunod nito.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: But opportunity must come with trust.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: As more Filipinos transact, communicate, work, study, and receive government services online,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: digital space safer and more trustworthy. I want to raise one issue that goes directly to

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: that responsibility. Over the past year, several members of the House have sought

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: government assistance concerning social media content they reported as fake,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: false, manipulated, defamatory, or otherwise harmful. These include requests

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: involving fabricated stories, altered images, AI-generated content, allegations

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: of corruption, personal attacks, and potentially threatening statements. Some

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: content was removed, but in a number of cases, the reported material remains

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: online even after referral, preservation, or review. One of the cases involves our

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: colleague, Congressman Miro Quimbo. His office alone referred 197 Facebook

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: links involving content directed against former Representative Stella Quimbo

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: and her family. According to the report furnished to us, these links were

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: monitored and validated, and the relevant digital material was preserved, but

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: reported content remained online after Meta found no violation of its

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: community standards. This raises a larger question which goes beyond the members

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: What happens? How does the Agency help? Do we have a solution? Sino mananagot sa proseso?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: At paano natin sisiguraduhin na may malinaw, mabilis, at transparent na tugon dito?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Because if this happens to members of Congress, what more the ordinary Filipino?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: We must make sure, and be equally clear, that government should not become an arbiter,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: of what opinions people may express online. Criticism of public officials is part of democratic

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: life, but manipulated media, impersonation, fraud, threats, coordinated deceptive activity,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: and other unlawful online conduct present a different problem, and require effective

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: institutional response, consistent with freedom of expression and due process. And for that

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Center, the consolidated complaints supporting materials received from members

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: from the House. And I am likewise furnishing META a copy for its appropriate review.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: I ask the DICT and CIC to review these cases individually, and to report to this committee

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: on what action has been taken and what remains pending, what further action may be taken,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: within their respective mandates and what legal technical institutional or

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: policy gaps may be preventing an effective response we also request meta

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: or we are requesting method to review the reported content under its

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: applicable policies and explain the disposition of referrals where

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: appropriate and clarify for review or escalation mechanisms that are available

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: when reported content is found not to violate its community standards and

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: since representatives of meta have been requested also to attend this hearing I

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: hope we can hear from them directly as I cannot place the blame solely on CICC

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: and DICT for not being able to respond to many of the complaint complaints right

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: away not just from members of Congress but from members all over government as

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: well as from private sector in civil society

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: we examine the fiscal year twenty twenty seven budget and I would like to and I

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: would like the department to satisfy this committee on several fundamental

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: questions are our connectivity targets real measurable and felt on the ground

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: particularly in our schools in underserved communities are we

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: adequately protecting government systems critical infrastructure and Filipino

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: data do we have clear strategy for cybersecurity and artificial

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: intelligence, including the opportunities for Filipino workers and businesses?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Are our investments in digital government producing greater transparency,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And last, do our institutions have the capability, legal tools,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: to respond effectively to new risks that come with an increasingly digital society,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: These are all part of the same national project.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Connect the country, protect its data, secure its systems,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: use technology to make government more transparent,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: and make sure that the digital economy creates opportunities for Filipinos.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: The trust of the people should be equal to the service.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And the connection should not just be

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: With that, I now invite the Department to present its Fiscal Year 2027 proposal in detail.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: After the presentation, we will hear questions, concerns, and views of our colleagues.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Secretary Henry Aguda, you may now proceed with your presentation.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Good afternoon, our budget sponsor, Congressman Brian Poe.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Maraming salamat po uli sa pangalawang taon na po natin na pinagtatrabahuhan ng budget.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: The Honorable Vice Chairs and Members of the House Committee on Appropriations,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: our distinguished members of the House of Representatives,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: fellow public servants, ladies and gentlemen.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: On behalf of the Department of Information, Communications, Technology,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: and our attached agencies, the CICC, the NPC,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Maraming salamat po for this opportunity to present our proposed budget for Fiscal Year 2027.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: At the DICT, we believe that every peso invested in ICT must translate into concrete and meaningful benefits for the Filipino.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Tulad po ng nasabi ng ating Chair at ang aming sponsor, hindi lang kailangan connected, kailangan napapakinabangan.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Our direction for Fiscal Year 2027 is

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: anchored on the DICT strategic framework.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: D is for Digital First Economy.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: We want to equip Filipinos with the skills, opportunities, and enabling environment they need to participate and succeed in an increasingly digital economy.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: I is for Inclusive Tech for All.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: This means expanding reliable and affordable connectivity

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: sa GIDA areas. C is for championing cybersecurity and data privacy. As more Filipinos

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: businesses and government services move online, we must make our digital environment safer,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: more resilient, and more trusted. Connectivity and digitalization must always go hand in hand

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: with cyber security and protection of our people's data. At kamakailan po, mainit-init

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: ang usipin natin sa social media at sa mga NVE situation po. Kabilin-bilinan ng ating

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Pangulo, walang kabataan na dapat maiwan at walang kabataan na dapat mapahamak.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: And T is for transparency and governance. We want technology to make government simpler,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: faster, and more transparent, and more responsive to our citizens so that our citizens spend

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: And more time benefiting from the services of what government provides. Kaya po nandyan

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: po ang ating E-Gov app, nandyan po ang E-LGU, at marami pang mga sistema para hindi na

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: pumipila ang ating mga kababayan, kundi nasiservisuhan na mas mabilis. Because ultimately,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: digital transformation is not simply about technology, it is about people. Ang tunay

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: na sukatan nito ay kung maaabot at nararamdaman ba ng ating mga kababayan ang benepisyon ng

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: teknolohiya. And before we proceed to the numbers and programs, we would first like

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: to hear from some of the Philippine

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: At the heart of our work, may maiksi lang pong AVP na papakita. Maiksi lang naman po yan, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: Presentation video
segments.text: Ang present natin ngayon is halos lahat nangyayari nasa internet. Kapag wala kang internet, parang mapag-iiwanan ka.

segments.speaker: Presentation video
segments.text: Ang pre-Wi-Fi po sa amin ay bihirang bihira po. Kami po ay kasalukuyang kumukonekta gamit po ng data sa aming mga telepono.

segments.speaker: Presentation video
segments.text: Actually, before po, nung wala pa pong DICT po, yung ginagawa po ng mga tao po dito, pumupunta pa po sila sa taas ng hundok po.

segments.speaker: Presentation video
segments.text: Without centralized services, agencies would need to make independent investments in hardware, which is quite expensive.

segments.speaker: Presentation video
segments.text: Sa loob ng ilang linggo, paggamit namin ng DICT by ANC, nagdala ito ng pagbabago.

segments.speaker: Presentation video
segments.text: Lalo lalo na sa aming pagtuturo, mas naging engaging ang aming talakayan.

segments.speaker: Presentation video
segments.text: Mas aktibo na nakikilabok ang amin.

segments.speaker: Presentation video
segments.text: These services deliver value far beyond subscription-based infrastructure.

segments.speaker: Presentation video
segments.text: They enable government agencies like ours, particularly those with limited resources and manpower, to actively participate in digital transformation.

segments.speaker: Presentation video
segments.text: This kind of communication equipment is going to help people communicate in a time of crisis.

segments.speaker: Presentation video
segments.text: One of the biggest challenges is to know where to send help, who needs the help, and how to get it to people.

segments.speaker: Presentation video
segments.text: Malaking tulong talaga siya sa amin, and I also hope that this project can be expanded farther, and that internet connectivity will continue to improve, especially in farther barangays where the signal is limited.

segments.speaker: Presentation video
segments.text: This is going to be the success factor that is going to save lives and change lives.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Yan po isang maiksing video lang para sa DICT.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Bago po namin puntahan ng mga numero,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: bigyan ko lang po siguro ako ng konting personal na mensahe po ng pasasalamat.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Pasasalamat po dahil pangalawang budget hearing ko na po ito.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Una po sa Pangulo, sa kanyang vision at sa kanyang suporta sa DICT,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: sa mga sumusuporta po namin sa buong kongreso po,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: malaking bagay po ang mga batas na naipasan nyo.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Yung konektadong Pinoy, malaking nagawa po niya sa industriya ng telecommunications.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Hindi man siya nakasama sa budget namin.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Pero gusto ko pong ihayag sa committee na nasa 2.4 billion US dollars po

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: ang committed investment ng telecoms industry ngayong taon po.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Yan po ay nasa between the 2 to 3 billion na inaasahan natin na manggagaling sa kanila.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Ang pagpapasa nyo po ng e-governance act na ngayon ay magiging full speed ahead na po.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Yan po ang magpapadali at magiging efficient po ang servisyo ng ating pamahalaan.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: At sa mga oversight committees na lahukan po namin,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: umaasa po kami yung mga susunod na batas,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: aayos po yung mga iba pa nating mga mas matitinding haharapin sa cyber security, social media, etc.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Sa mga kasama ko po sa DICT at ang mga attached agency, CICC, NPC, NTC,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: tumataas po ang kumpiyansa ko sa servisyo ng mga tao sa gobyerno.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Masisipag, magagalang, at professional po ang mga tao sa DICT.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Lahat po ay pwede nyo lapitan at lahat po ay hindi tatanggi sa pagsisilbi sa bayan.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Doon po sa ating mga kababayan, lalo na po yung mga matagal nang naghihintay ng connectivity.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Salamat po sa inyong pagtangkilik sa servisyo ng DICT.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Salamat po at alam namin naghintay kayo ng matagal.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: At kayo po ang dahilan kung bakit ngayong budget season na ito,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: bawat piso na hihingin namin sa Kongreso ay ilalaan namin sa pagsisilbisyo sa inyo.

segments.text: Afterwards, with the permission of the Chair,

segments.text: I will now turn over the detailed presentation to our Undersecretary for Support Services,

segments.text: that are already translating our investments in ICT into tangible benefits for the Filipino people.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Mr. Chair, a copy of our full-page presentation is provided to each member of this committee for your perusal.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: I will go over the landmark accomplishments and at the same time the detailed NEP for 2027.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Mr. Chair, one of the most significant accomplishments is bringing government services

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: directly into the hands of millions of Filipinos through the eGov Super App.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Today, we are proud to say that we have 61 million plus downloads,

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: More than 56 million verified accounts and over 1.2 billion eGovDX transactions

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: These include everyday services such as PhilHealth, eTravel, eCov, eTrabajo, eLGU, and eReport,

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: alongside more than 92 million digital national IDs issued and over 300 million digital ID transactions.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: More importantly, digital government is now institutionalized through the

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: e-Governance Act and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Instead of citizens having to navigate government,

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: we are bringing government closer to the citizen through one increasingly integrated digital ecosystem.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Alongside expanding digital services, we have pursued reforms that make it faster and easier

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: to build telecommunications infrastructure, ranging from streamlined permitting

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: and longer regulatory validity to infrastructure sharing and open access.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: These reforms help enable expansion of telecommunications towers from close to 18,000 in 2020 to about 35,000 in 2023,

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: while the number of connected Filipinos increased from 77 million in July 2022 to about 99 million by June of 2026.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: With the help of the Konektadong Pinoy Act, we are building on these gains by promoting greater competition,

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: infrastructure sharing, and more efficient network deployment.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: As government becomes more digital, connectivity must expand with it so more Filipinos can actually participate and benefit.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: These infrastructure and policy reforms are translating into measurable improvements in the everyday internet experience of Filipinos.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Since 2022, mobile download speeds have more than doubled, while fixed broadband speeds have also improved.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: At the same time, Filipinos are getting significantly

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: more data for every peso spent.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Most importantly, Mr. Chair, access is expanding.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: The share of Filipinos using internet increased from 25.4% in 2019 to about 67% in 2024,

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: while households with internet access increased from 17.7% to about 48.8%.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: So the story across these first three accomplishments is connected.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: We are digitalizing government, removing barriers to connectivity,

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: and working to ensure that faster and more affordable internet allows more Filipinos to actually participate in our digital transformation.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: And we are applying that same principle of digital transformation to improve specific government services.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: When better connectivity is paired with digital government, we can transform even very specific services that directly affect people's livelihoods.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: A good example is the PIMEDES portal,

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: What used to take an average of three months through a manual process can now be completed digitally in about five days.

segments.text: To date, Mr. Chair, the NSOC has monitored about 6.7 billion security alerts, demonstrating both the scale of threats we face and the importance of maintaining a strong national cyber defense capability.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Our investment in the next-generation hybrid NSOC will therefore sustain and strengthen 24-7 protection across disconnected agencies. Because our digital transformation can only succeed if Filipinos can also trust that the government systems and services they increasingly depend on are secure and resilient.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: But a secure and connected digital Philippines is only meaningful if Filipinos also have the skills to participate in it.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: DICT has reached about 695,000 Filipinos through free and accessible ICT capacity development, providing free training in areas such as AI, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, digital work, entrepreneurship, and digital literacy.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Through our DTCs, or Digital Transformation Centers, and initiatives such as SPARC, we are also bringing these opportunities closer to communities.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Including support that has helped form 35 local freelancer organizations nationwide.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Our goal is to complete the chain, connect our people, protect them online, equip them with relevant digital skills, and ultimately open more opportunities for work, enterprise, and participation in digital economy.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: As we expand these programs, we are also continuously improving how we deliver them.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: A good example is our free public internet access program.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Through improved technology, contracting, and connectivity arrangement, we have achieved reported cost efficiencies of up to 70%, Mr. Chair, while continuing to expand access, particularly in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Today, free Wi-Fi has reached about 10.37 million unique beneficiaries with 127.49 million user sessions.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: At an estimated cost of about 22.4 pesos per unique beneficiary, and that's per month.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: This reflects how we want the ICT to work.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Expand what delivers, impact, measure performance, learn from implementation, and continuously find ways to deliver more value for every peso entrusted to us.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: And that is the principle we will carry moving forward.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Not simply to do more, but to do better.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: More efficiently, more effectively, and with greater success.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: And with greater impact for the Filipino people.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Mr. Chair, I will now proceed to the Fiscal Year 2027 National Expenditure Program and present how the proposed budget will support the Department's priorities and commitments for the coming year.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: For the Fiscal Year 2027, the proposed budget for the ICT and its attached agencies totals 19.491 billion.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Of this amount, 17.6 billion is for the DICT Office of the Secretary.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: While 594.4 million is provided for CICC, 505.4 million for the National Privacy Commission, and 790 million for the National Telecommunications Commission.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Across the entire department, the budget consists of 1.692 billion for personal services, 13.9 billion for MOE, and 3.892 billion for capital outlay.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: In closing, Mr. Chair, and the honorable members of this committee, what we have presented today is more than a list of programs, targets, and budget figures.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Ito po ang direksyon ng DICT, mula connectivity, digital government, cybersecurity, digital skills, and jobs, hanggang sa pagbuo ng isang mas modernong gobyerno na tunay na naramdaman ng ating mga kababayan.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: With the support of the Congress for our Fiscal Year 2027 budget, we commit to translate every peso.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: entrusted to DICT into better connectivity, better digital services, greater digital opportunities, and concrete benefits for every Filipino.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Support Services Heherson M. Asiddao
segments.text: Maraming salamat po, and magandang hapon po sa inyong lahat.

segments.text: Lalo na pag walang interference, naka 200-250 Mbps for upload and download.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: And malaking tulong po ito para sa ating mga schools.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Lalo na actually galing lang po ako sa DepEd.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: And ang ating learning crisis ay kailangan din talaga na may digital help para doon.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: But I'd wanted to ask, I think, a rather basic question.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: I know that EO 119 has been signed for a data framework.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: I know that DBM has UACS codes.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: But is there a data standard for entire bureaucracy?

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Mr. Chair, Your Honor, by next week, we will convene the technical working group for the EO 119.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: That is an inter-agency technical working group.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: And we will craft the standards, Mr. Chair, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: I was just looking sana kay USEC Sara kanina.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Because she knows the details eh.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: But the technical working group starts meeting this week.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Mr. Chair, and thank you, Mr. Secretary.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Now I wanted to ask, because data standards are important.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: When we look at DBM as well, it should be, you know, may UACS yan, unified identifiers.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Would we go from the formulation of the NEP to the MGA, to SAROs, disbursements?

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: I mean, I used to trade in the crypto space.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: And I know, I'm a bit exposed about blockchain.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: And we all know that it is a ledger, a distributed ledger, that is encrypted by a cryptographic hash.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: I wanted to ask, because I know that this is being pushed as well.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Kadena, which I am a co-author, do you believe that this is feasible for our government?

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: And how much do you think it would cost?

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Mr. Chair, Your Honor, I think the concept of Kadena, the CA, the Kadena bill, is feasible in our government.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: As to the amount, I think it depends on how the legislature will craft the laws.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Whether it's public chain, private chain, and the extent to which it will be implemented.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: But I think whatever the amount is, if it achieves the objective of transparency in government, it will be worth it, Mr. Chair, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Mr. Chair and Mr. Secretary, do you believe that Kadena will solve corruption in the Philippines?

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Mr. Chair, Your Honor, Kadena is a tool to curb corruption.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: As with all transparency portals that we're implementing right now.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Ultimately, it's how effective the tool is implemented.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: I think it can minimize corruption.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: And when we talk about Kadena,

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: and it's supposed to curb corruption,

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: it's supposed to curb corruption, I understand.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: But I know that Bayani Chain has also made on-chain for free.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Do you believe that this is possible?

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: That we can also have a very minimal budget for this in case it does pass or in case that we do pursue it?

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: the one that Bayani Chain did was a free chain.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Basically, what they did is just onboarded the published budget of 2025 into a public chain.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: I think the approach of uploading the published budget on any chain is feasible and that's free.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: The question there is if you establish a system end-to-end from NEP to expenditure.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: And more importantly, which is I'm a big proponent of,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Because if you want to track every peso that comes out of the government,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: the easier way of doing it is to just tokenize all of the peso.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: And then, you can now follow the provenance.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Now, if that's the ambition that we want,

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: I think that would be the better solution.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Because right now, each citizen can account for every peso that goes out of the government.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: But it will take a lot of work, Mr. Chair, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: So it seems, Mr. Chair and Mr. Secretary,

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: it seems that once we make it transparent,

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: it may have the same effect but we have to ensure that data going in is also as credible, correct?

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Mr. Chair, I'd like to ask about EGov.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: And I think I wanted to ask,

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Because I know that it collects government data and as well as citizens' data.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Who owns EGov, the source code, Mr. Secretary?

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Mr. Chair, Your Honor, the ownership is with the government.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: I think earlier conversation, I have USEC Admiral who mentioned that

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: we're the custodian and owner of the source code at this point.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: And how many active monthly users?

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Mr. Chair, Your Honor, maybe I should turn it over to USEC Admiral for the details

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: so that it's consistent with his earlier statement.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: USEC, you may share the numbers once more?

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: So right now, Mr. Chair, since we already have 61 million downloads with 56 million unique users,

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: our average daily download, Mr. Chair, is about 70,000 to 100,000 a day.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: So approximately, Mr. Chair, for monthly active downloads,

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: about around 3 million downloads monthly, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Mr. Chair and USEC, how much is that per user, per transaction is the cost to run EGov?

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: In terms of maybe economic impact on the current budget that we have,

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: approximately, Mr. Chair, around 9 pesos per user, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: And how does EGov get funded?

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: For the development, Mr. Chair, since we build this internally,

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: so we don't have any contractor developing and building EGov.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: Right now, Mr. Chair, we're only paying our own staff to do it.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: Right now, we have about approximately more than 30 programmers

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Okay. So, Mr. Chair, you said 9 pesos per user, correct?

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: For comparing our current budget, EGov budget, to the users, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Okay. So all internal and no line item budget, correct?

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: And there are no private companies or contractors working?

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: Yes, Mr. Chair, for the development, for the R&D.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: The one that's only paying, Mr. Chair, is actually the subscription of our storage,

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: our cloud, service security, and other non-software developers' expenses.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Okay. And where is this cloud stored?

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: Right now, Mr. Chair, it's stored in Singapore.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: So since we're using public cloud services, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Okay. So what company in Singapore, if I may ask?

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: We also have several services stored in Google.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: We have some in the Google Cloud and also some also in our current existing co-locations, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Okay. Mr. Chair, so it seems that the data of our Filipino people are in AWS or Google Cloud in Singapore, no?

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Mr. Chair, I'd like to ask the department if are you amenable that we have sovereign data centers to house our data?

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr.
segments.text: So we're supposed to own it, manage it locally.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Alam kong time's up na rin ako.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: But siguro dahil Department of Tourism is next, yung digital nomad visa na lang, ano po yung status po nun?

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Tsaka sana meron tayong mas maraming digital nomads na makapunta sa ating bansa.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Who do I recognize from DICT?

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Actually, we've been pushing the nomad visa.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: And we've been working closely with DICT.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: Working closely with the Department of Foreign Affairs.

segments.speaker: DICT Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda
segments.text: But the latest, I think, if I can pass it on to USEC Sarah on the latest status of that initiative.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Policy, Legal, and Communications Sarah Maria Q. Sison
DICT Undersecretary for Policy, Legal, and Communications Sarah Maria Q. Sison
segments.text: So the Office of the Undersecretary for Policy is working closely with our Cybersecurity Bureau together with the Department of Foreign Affairs.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Policy, Legal, and Communications Sarah Maria Q. Sison
segments.text: It is still in the planning and consultation stage.

segments.speaker: DICT Undersecretary for Policy, Legal, and Communications Sarah Maria Q. Sison
segments.text: But we will give an update as soon as we have our timeline because there's a lot of cybersecurity issues involved, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Chair, and to the Department of Information, Communications, and Technology.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: I look forward to much more of your work.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: I'd like to congratulate Zach Henry and the whole DICT team.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: I believe that you have a track record.

segments.speaker: Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez
segments.text: And we hope that more budget for the DICT because here we are, dear colleagues, compared to our Asian and global partners.
